title: ICAB C6 - Business Laws
summary: Covers Companies Act 1994, Negotiable Instruments Act 1881, Partnership Act 1932, Contract Act 1872, Sale of Goods Act 1930, and Labour Act 2006.

all.name: Full Syllabus Tracker
all.blurb: Official 2025 Syllabus chapter and topic tracker for Business Laws. Track your study progress across all syllabus areas.

stages.title: Area 1: Companies Act 1994
stages.name: Area 1: Companies Act 1994
stages.description: Company incorporation, Memorandum & Articles, shares, directors, and basic corporate governance.

nodes.name: Company Formation, MoA, AoA & Directors
nodes.description: Types of companies (private, public, one person company); incorporation process with RJSC; Memorandum and Articles of Association; doctrine of ultra vires and indoor management; appointment, qualification, and duties of directors; meetings (AGM, EGM) and resolutions.
topics: Classification of companies: Private limited, Public limited, One Person Company (OPC)
Registration and incorporation steps with RJSC
Memorandum of Association: Clauses and alteration procedures
Articles of Association: Regulations, alteration by special resolution
Doctrine of Ultra Vires and Doctrine of Constructive Notice / Indoor Management
Directors: Legal position, appointment, disqualification, retirement by rotation
Company meetings: Statutory meeting, Annual General Meeting (AGM), Extra-ordinary General Meeting (EGM)
Ordinary and special resolutions, quorum, and voting
learningOutcomes: Explain the legal characteristics and incorporation procedures of companies.
Apply the doctrines of ultra vires and indoor management to contracts.
Determine legal requirements for directors' appointments and shareholder meetings.
checklists: Review RJSC incorporation steps and required documentation
Memorize AGM statutory timeline and notice periods
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

stages.title: Area 2: Negotiable Instruments Act 1881
stages.name: Area 2: Negotiable Instruments Act 1881
stages.description: Promissory notes, bills of exchange, cheques, crossing, endorsement, and dishonor under Section 138.

nodes.name: Promissory Notes, Bills of Exchange & Cheque Dishonor
nodes.description: Definition and characteristics of negotiable instruments; promissory note vs bill of exchange vs cheque; holder and holder in due course; negotiation, endorsement, and crossing of cheques; dishonour of cheques and legal remedies under Section 138.
topics: Essential characteristics of negotiable instruments
Promissory notes vs Bills of exchange vs Cheques
Holder in due course: Rights, privileges, and protection
Endorsement types: Blank, full, restrictive, conditional
Types of crossing of cheques: General crossing vs Special crossing and protection to paying banker
Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency of funds (Section 138 NI Act): Legal notice, timelines, and penal consequences
learningOutcomes: Distinguish between promissory notes, bills of exchange, and cheques.
Identify the rights of a holder in due course.
Explain the legal procedure and notice requirements for cheque dishonor under Section 138.
checklists: Memorize Section 138 statutory timeline (30 days notice, 30 days filing)
Practice identifying valid endorsements and crossing types
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

stages.title: Area 3: Partnership Act 1932
stages.name: Area 3: Partnership Act 1932
stages.description: Partnership nature, mutual rights, duties, dissolution, and effects of non-registration.

nodes.name: Partnership Formation, Relations & Dissolution
nodes.description: Definition and essential elements of partnership; mutual agency test; rights and duties of partners inter se; implied authority of a partner; position of a minor; dissolution of firm; consequences of non-registration of firm.
topics: Definition of partnership: Agreement, business, profit sharing, mutual agency
True test of partnership (Section 6 - Cox v. Hickman principle)
Rights, duties, and liabilities of partners to one another and third parties
Implied authority of a partner and statutory restrictions
Admission, retirement, expulsion, and insolvency of a partner
Position of a minor admitted to benefits of partnership
Dissolution of a partnership firm by agreement, notice, contingencies, or court order
Consequences of non-registration of a firm (disability to sue third parties)
learningOutcomes: Apply the mutual agency test to identify partnership relationships.
Determine the extent of a partner's implied authority.
Explain grounds for dissolution and legal impact of non-registration.
checklists: Analyze court order dissolution grounds under Section 44
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

stages.title: Area 4: Contract Act 1872 & Sale of Goods Act 1930
stages.name: Area 4: Contract Act 1872 & Sale of Goods Act 1930
stages.description: Offer, acceptance, consideration, free consent, breach of contract, conditions and warranties.

nodes.name: Contract Essentials, Breach & Sale of Goods
nodes.description: Essentials of a valid contract (Section 10); offer, acceptance, consideration; capacity to contract; free consent (coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation, mistake); discharge of contract; remedies for breach of contract (damages); Sale of Goods Act: Sale vs agreement to sell, conditions vs warranties, doctrine of caveat emptor.
topics: Elements of a valid contract: Offer, acceptance, lawful consideration, intention
Vitiating factors: Coercion, Undue Influence, Fraud, Misrepresentation, Mistake
Void agreements vs voidable contracts vs illegal agreements
Discharge of contracts: By performance, agreement, frustration/impossibility, breach
Remedies for breach of contract: Damages (ordinary, special, nominal), specific performance, injunction
Sale of Goods Act: Sale vs agreement to sell, transfer of property/risk
Conditions and Warranties: Implied conditions as to title, description, quality/fitness
Doctrine of Caveat Emptor (buyer beware) and statutory exceptions
learningOutcomes: Evaluate validity of contracts under Contract Act 1872.
Determine available remedies for contractual breach.
Distinguish between conditions and warranties in sale of goods.
checklists: Review Hadley v. Baxendale rule for contractual damages
List implied conditions under Sale of Goods Act 1930
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)

stages.title: Area 5: Labour Act 2006 & Employment Regulations
stages.name: Area 5: Labour Act 2006 & Employment Regulations
stages.description: Employment conditions, leave, working hours, misconduct, retrenchment, and workers' participation fund.

nodes.name: Employment Conditions, Termination & WPPF
nodes.description: Classification of workers (permanent, probationer, casual); service book and appointment letter; working hours, overtime, annual leave; termination of employment (discharge, dismissal, retrenchment, lay-off); misconduct disciplinary process; Workers' Profit Participation Fund (WPPF).
topics: Worker classification under Bangladesh Labour Act 2006
Conditions of employment: Working hours (8h/day, 48h/week), overtime rate (double ordinary wage)
Leave entitlements: Casual leave, sick leave, annual leave with wages, maternity benefit
Termination modalities: Retrenchment, discharge, dismissal for misconduct
Disciplinary proceedings: Charge-sheet, inquiry committee, right of defense
Workers' Profit Participation Fund (WPPF): Participation fund and welfare fund allocation (5% of net profit)
learningOutcomes: Explain statutory working hours and leave entitlements.
Describe the legal procedure for dismissal on grounds of misconduct.
State employer obligations regarding WPPF establishment.
checklists: Memorize misconduct disciplinary inquiry process timeline
Review maternity benefit calculation and notice rules
resources: Relevant Acts & Standards (IFRS / ISA / Tax Acts)
